name: Pane
text: The real risk isn’t ambient light—it’s that auto-switching still assumes users *prefer* the light theme when glare hits, not that they *need* it. A better alternative: let users pick a *fixed* theme (dark/light) and add a manual override button that persists until toggled again—no assumptions, no delays. Settle it with a 5-user hallway test: measure how often they override the auto-switch in glare.

name: Pane
text: The real risk isn’t manual effort—it’s that users in bright rooms won’t bother toggling, leaving them squinting at a dark screen. A better alternative: default to dark, but add a *persistent* ambient light sensor that only *suggests* a light theme via a subtle banner—no auto-switch, no override, just a clear prompt users can accept or dismiss. Settle it with A/B testing: measure completion time and error rates in high-glare vs. low-glare scenarios.
